cards.explanation: The altar is for burning incense. God says to make “…an altar of acacia wood for the burning of incense.” It's right there in the very first verse, so no digging required, friends. Aaron burns the incense every morning and again at twilight (Exodus 30:7-8). Once a year he also makes atonement on its horns (Exodus 30:10).

The answer is that God will meet with Moses there. God says the altar goes before the veil and the mercy seat, “…where I will meet with you.” He's speaking to Moses, Israel's leader. It's a special spot, so it's worth getting the placement exactly right, friends.

The answer is True! God says Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), “…must burn the incense perpetually before the LORD for the generations to come.” The text has Aaron burning it every morning when he tends the lamps, and again when he sets up the lamps at twilight (Exodus 30:7-8). Generations to come? That's a longer run than any batch I've ever baked.

The answer is False. God says, “On this altar you must not offer unauthorized incense or a burnt offering or grain offering…” So burnt offerings are a no here, friends. I've put the wrong dough in the wrong pan before, but God's instructions here are very clear.

The word is plague. God says, “Then no plague will come upon them when they are numbered.” Each man pays a ransom for his life when he's counted. It's a short verse with a lot of weight in it, friends.

The atonement money is for the service of the Tent of Meeting. God says to take the atonement money and “…use it for the service of the Tent of Meeting.” He also says it serves as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD. And remember, friends, the rich don't give more than a half shekel and the poor don't give less (Exodus 30:15).

The basin's water is for Aaron and his sons to wash. They are to wash their hands and feet in it, and God says to set it between the Tent of Meeting and the altar and put water in it. A basin of water for hands and feet, and it carries a serious instruction, friends. Whenever they enter the Tent or approach the altar, they must wash (Exodus 30:20).

The reason is so that they will not die. God says, “…they must wash with water so that they will not die.” He says it again in verse 21, friends. He also calls it “…a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants for the generations to come.” That's serious business, and it's worth slowing down for.

God tells Moses to make a sacred anointing oil. He says, “Prepare from these a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer…” The spices go together with olive oil in this blend, friends. It's a special recipe, and the instructions are specific.
The answer is True! God says to consecrate these things “…so that they will be most holy. Whatever touches them shall be holy.” That's a strong statement, friends. They're set apart in a serious way.

The word is priests. God tells Moses to anoint Aaron and his sons and “…consecrate them to serve Me as priests.” The same oil that anoints the furnishings anoints them too, friends. Priests is the word.

The answer is False. God says, “…you must not make anything like it with the same formula.” He also says, “It is holy, and it must be holy to you.” I'd never copy a formula God says to leave alone, friends.

He will be cut off from his people. God says anyone who mixes perfume like the sacred oil or puts it on an outsider “…shall be cut off from his people.” That's a serious warning, friends. God is showing how holy this oil is.

The answer is False. God says, “You are never to use this formula to make incense for yourselves; you shall regard it as holy to the LORD.” Anyone who makes it to enjoy its fragrance “…shall be cut off from his people.” That's a serious line, friends.
